release_policy.rule_scope: DOMAIN only; DOMAIN-SUFFIX is never generated automatically
release_policy.approval_rule: A domain is assigned only when at least two distinct configured publishers and source groups currently list the exact domain under the same declared policy, and all deterministic local checks pass. Incomplete lineage is recorded but is not a blanket veto. No AI, model API, or manual per-domain review is used.

approval_criteria.description: At least two distinct current publisher sources and source groups list the exact domain under the same DIRECT, PROXY or REJECT policy; source identity, policy-evidence type and snapshot hash must match the registry.
Existing first-match domain rules, conditional AND/OR/NOT rules, DOMAIN-KEYWORD, URL-REGEX, skip-proxy and protected-domain checks must all pass.

mandatory_vetoes: Any exact or suffix rule with a different effective policy blocks publication
Any unresolved conditional AND/OR/NOT overlap blocks publication
Any critical-function protection-list match blocks publication
Any malformed source snapshot, excessive source drift, duplicate ledger key or failed validator pauses the batch
Single-label root suffix entries are excluded; duplicate entries are deduplicated
release_policy.review_status: A single-source candidate or a candidate below the two-publisher corroboration threshold remains REVIEW; cross-policy conflicts and critical-function risks are held.
release_policy.publish_gate: No automatic writes to original or canonical baseline. Derived output only.
release_policy.confidence_interpretation: Operational evidence score, not a statistical probability or guarantee of safe blocking.
release_policy.direct_proxy_policy: DIRECT and PROXY are active through the registered ACL4SSR/Clash-FX and ACL4SSR/sve1r source pairs; only domain-level corroborated entries are eligible for publication.

managed_config_guard.description: Current user-managed subscription file; automation must not modify it.
